Query card journeys

Every status’s card, the main action it offers, and what happens when you take it, followed by where each journey breaks or falls short of best in class. Walked in the current prototype at 1512 × 900 on 6 Nov.

6Broken: the writer can’t finish, or ends up somewhere wrong
8Fall short: they work, but take more effort or give less than they should
3Polish: small visual slips against your rulings

The journey for each status

What the card says, the action it puts first, and what that action does today.

Offer

Tom Ellery made an offer. Footer: “Answer the offer · 1 day left”.

Main actionAnswer the offer

Opens the generic “Something changed since” list. Every choice is greyed out or doesn’t fit. Nothing can be saved.

BrokenB1

Partial or full requested

Clara asked for a partial 36 days ago. Footer: “Send the partial · 8 days late”.

Main actionMark partial sent

A two-step form, with a confirm screen before Save. It works, but it opens scrolled to the bottom with its fields hidden. The full’s deadline is made up.

Falls shortB3 · F1 · B6

Nudge due

Priya hasn’t replied by the reply date. Footer: Nudge, plus a Close it link.

Main actionNudge

Two steps to log something you did outside the app, with no help writing the nudge. Afterwards the footer reads “0 days since your nudge”.

Falls shortF1 · F5

Watch and wait

Sophie has the partial. Footer: “Waiting on Sophie · reply expected by 10 Oct”.

Main actionRecord a response

A list of eight choices, half of them greyed out. The list is missing R&R and other reply types, and captures none of what the agent said.

BrokenB5 · B6 · F2 · F8

Daniel is four weeks past his reply date. Footer: Nudge, plus a Close it link.

Main actionNudge

The same journey as Nudge due, so it has the same gaps.

Closed

George passed. Footer: “Closed · George passed · 5 Oct” and Reopen.

Main actionReopen

Goes straight to a confirm screen that says “You’re adding · Removed Passed”. It never asks why you’re reopening, and puts the query back on a reply date that has already passed.

BrokenB4

These sit on every card, whatever its status.

Agent tabWorks well: reply time, what they ask for, wishlist, contact. A few labels are uppercase mono.FineP1

EscapeInside a form, Escape opens the “What needs changing?” choice instead of going back to the card. Pressed again, it does nothing.BrokenB2

Broken6

The writer can’t finish the job, or the app records the wrong thing.

B1

Answering an offer is a dead end

Broken

What happens

The footer’s main button, Answer the offer, opens the generic “Something changed since” form. Its preview is empty, and every choice in its list is either greyed out (“Offer is already on the timeline”) or doesn’t fit. You can’t accept or decline, ask for time, or set the agent’s deadline. The “Tell other agents” step from v152.1 isn’t in the prototype either.

Best in class

An offer is the one moment a writer most needs hand-holding. Give it its own journey. First, the offer: date, the agent’s deadline, terms and a note. Then what you’re doing: accept, decline, or take time to decide. Taking time sets a deadline and opens Tell other agents. That step lists everyone still holding the book, with a ready-made “I’ve had an offer” email for each, which you copy and then mark as told. Accepting closes or withdraws the rest in one confirmed step.

B2

Escape and Back don’t do what you expect

Broken

What happens

In a form, Escape doesn’t return to the card: it opens the “What needs changing?” choice. A second press does nothing, so the only way out is ✕ or Cancel. The back link changes too: “← Back to Clara’s query” on one screen, “← What needs changing?” on the next.

Best in class

One rule everywhere. Escape and the back link both go up one level: form → card → closed. If you’ve typed something, you’re asked once before it’s thrown away. The back link always names where it goes.

B3

The form opens with its fields out of sight

Broken

What happens

Mark partial sent opens scrolled to the bottom, so the title, steps and instructions are off the top. The date and “What you’re sending” fields sit below a large preview that is mostly empty space. Scrolled to the top, about 60% of the first screen is an empty box. You can’t see what you’re being asked until you scroll inside the card.

Best in class

Lead with the question and keep everything above the fold: what happened, when, and what went. Make the preview a slim strip showing the bubble you’re about to add, the way a chat app shows a reply before you send it. Pin the action to the footer, where the card’s own action already sits.

B4

Reopen assumes the wrong thing, and says it confusingly

Broken

What happens

Reopen skips straight to the confirm screen: “You’re adding · Removed Passed”, so it’s adding and removing in the same breath. It never asks why. Either the pass was recorded by mistake, which is a Fix, or George came back, with an R&R or a request for more. Instead, it restores the old wait with a reply due on 14 Oct, which has already gone by.

Best in class

Ask one question: “Recorded by mistake” (undo the pass, no new step) or “George got back in touch” (record what he asked for, with today’s date). Either way the result is written in plain words: “The pass comes off. It goes back to waiting on George.”

B5

Record a response is missing real replies, and mixes in your own steps

Broken

What happens

The list offers partial, full, offer and passed, plus “You nudged” and “You closed it”, which aren’t replies at all. There’s no Revise & resubmit, no “asked for something else” (more pages, a synopsis, a call), no “withdrew”, and no way to tell a form rejection from a personal one. Options that can’t apply stay in the list, greyed out with explanations.

Best in class

Title it “What did Sophie say?” and list only replies that can happen next, most likely first: asked for the full, passed, R&R, an offer, asked for something else. Your own steps (sent, nudged, closed) live on the footer, where they already are.

B6

None of what the agent said is captured

Broken

What happens

Asked for the full: the form records the date and the material, then makes up a deadline (“due to send your full by 22 Oct”, which is today plus 14 days). It never asks what the agent actually said. A pass has no reason, feedback or “open to future work”. An offer has no deadline. The thread can show quoted agent replies (v152.1), but nothing here lets you capture one.

Best in class

Every reply gets the same two optional fields: paste their reply, which becomes the quoted bubble, and the deadline they gave, which drives the footer, prefilled from their usual turnaround. Passes add “form or personal” and “open to future submissions”, which also feed the Wall of no.

Falls short8

These work, but take more steps, or capture less, than the best apps would.

F1

Routine steps take two screens

Falls short

What happens

Mark sent, Nudge and Close each go through a “What changes” screen and then Save. The preview is right for edits that ripple, but for the everyday case it’s a speed bump: you know what marking a partial sent means.

Best in class

For one-step actions, one tap confirms, with an undo toast (“Partial sent · Undo”) and the new bubble animating into the thread. Keep the “What changes” preview for edits that move dates or remove steps.

F2

Titles don’t match the button you pressed

Falls short

What happens

You press “Record a response” and land on “Something changed since”. The Nudge button opens “Log a nudge”, and the back link reads “What needs changing?”. These are app-speak labels, not the words on the button.

Best in class

Every title repeats the action in the writer’s words: “What did Sophie say?”, “Nudge Priya”, “Mark the partial sent”, “Close Priya’s query”.

F3

The pencil opens a three-way choice

Falls short

What happens

The pencil offers “Fix a mistake”, “Something changed since” and “Edit the query’s details”. The second repeats the footer and the first repeats the bubble Edit, so it’s an extra click and an extra decision.

Best in class

The pencil edits the query’s details directly: who, how, package, notes. Fixes happen on the bubble; new steps happen in the footer. Each control does one thing.

F4

Edit on a bubble opens the whole history

Falls short

What happens

Clicking ✎ Edit on one bubble opens every step as rows of dropdowns and dates. The clicked step is outlined, the rest sit on blue-grey panels that aren’t in the palette, and any step’s type can be changed by dropdown, which can break the history.

Best in class

Edit in place. The bubble turns into a small form for its date, materials, quoted reply and a delete option, and the rest of the thread stays put. “Edit the whole history” stays available as a link for the rare big fix.

F5

A nudge gets no help, and the footer reads oddly afterwards

Falls short

What happens

The writer has to go and write the nudge somewhere else, come back and log it. There’s no channel (email, QueryManager). After saving, the footer says “0 days since your nudge · quiet after 4 weeks”.

Best in class

Show a short, editable follow-up email (“Following up on my query for Murphy’s Day Out, sent 1 Jul…”) with Copy and Open in mail, then “I’ve sent it”. After saving, the footer reads “Nudged today · goes quiet on 5 Nov”.

F6

Close it never mentions a nudge

Falls short

What happens

From Nudge due, or Gone quiet with no nudge, Close it goes straight to closing as “no response”, even though the writer hasn’t followed up.

Best in class

One line above Save: “You haven’t nudged Priya. One polite follow-up often gets a reply.” Next to it, Nudge instead. Then let them close.

F7

The Materials tab can’t be changed

Falls short

What happens

It lists what went, but there’s no add, swap or remove here, so the question you asked before (“how are materials edited?”) is still open on this tab.

Best in class

Each row gets ✎. Free plan: edit the chips. Pro: change the package, or the version a sample came from. A “+ Add what you sent” link sits under the last row.

F8

Choices that can’t apply are still listed

Falls short

What happens

Greyed-out options with notes (“Partial requested is already on the timeline”, “You can’t send the full before it was requested”) take up half the list.

Best in class

Hide what can’t happen. If something is missing, a single “Something else…” at the bottom covers it.

Polish3

Small things that break rulings you’ve already made.

P1

Uppercase mono labels are back

Polish

What happens

“Who replied”, “What you did”, “Querying”, “Queried”, “Package” and “Last heard” are all uppercase mono eyebrows, the “AI tell” you’ve ruled out.

Best in class

Sentence case in the serif, or drop the label where the content says it.

P2

The draft preview uses the old nudge glyph

Polish

What happens

The bubble preview in the nudge form still shows the old ring, not the “!” in a ring.

Best in class

Use the thread’s glyph everywhere.

P3

“You’re adding · Full requested” is tinted pink

Polish

What happens

The summary chip uses the partial colour for a full request.

Best in class

Summary chips take the same reply-type tint as the bubble: blue for a full.

What I couldn’t test

  • Gone quiet after a nudge: the prototype has no query in this state, so the “Close it first” footer hasn’t been walked.
  • Tell other agents: it’s in the v152.1 build on dev but not in the prototype, so I couldn’t walk it here. If the dev version has its own problems, send me a screenshot.
  • Free plan and phone: not walked this round.

A proposed shape for the fix

  1. One action, one journey, titled with the button’s words. Mark sent, Nudge, Close, What did they say, Answer the offer, Reopen.
  2. Routine steps take one tap and offer Undo. The “What changes” preview is kept for edits that move dates or remove steps.
  3. Replies capture what the agent said: their words, their deadline, and, for a pass, form or personal.
  4. The offer gets its own guided journey, with Tell other agents built in.
  5. Edit in place: the bubble edits itself, the pencil edits details, and Escape always goes up one level.
